title: Germany – Construction works for plants, mining and manufacturing and for buildings relating to the oil and gas industry – Bau und Ausrüstung der Demonstrationsanlage MoorFaserWerk Malchin (Verbundprojekt MOOReturn)
description: Errichtung einer industriellen Aufbereitungsanlage zur Verarbeitung von Grasschnitt und Laub aus der Landschaftspflege zu pelletierten oder brikettierten Festbrennstoffen (Kapazität ca. 3.100 t/a) am Standort Industriegelände 6, 17139 Malchin, im Rahmen des vom BMEL über die FNR geförderten Verbundprojekts MOOReturn. Der Auftrag umfasst als Generalübernehmerleistung: Planung (einschließlich Genehmigungsplanung), Bauleistungen (Ertüchtigung der Bestandshalle inkl. Hallentore, Medienerschließung, brandschutztechnischer Ertüchtigung, Sozial- und Sanitärräume) sowie die Beschaffung und Montage sämtlicher Anlagenkomponenten der Prozesskette (Dosierung, Waschmaschine, Abtropftrommel, Feinzerkleinerung, Pressentwässerung, thermische Trocknung, Verdichtung). Die Vergabe als integrierte Gesamtleistung dient der Vermeidung von Schnittstellenrisiken und der Sicherstellung einer einheitlichen, vom Generalübernehmer verantworteten Anlagenkonformität. Die Umsetzung des Auftrags ist in aufeinander aufbauenden Leistungsstufen vorgesehen. Der Auftraggeber beabsichtigt, einzelne Leistungsstufen entsprechend dem Projektfortschritt abzurufen. Die Beauftragung weiterer Leistungsstufen erfolgt jeweils vorbehaltlich der Bereitstellung der Fördermittel sowie des Erreichens der definierten Projektmeilensteine. Ein Anspruch auf Beauftragung weiterer Leistungsstufen besteht nicht. Ausführliche Beschreibung des Beschaffungsvorhabens s. Anlage 1 unter folgendem Link: https://www.dbfz.de/fileadmin/Projektseiten/MooReturn/doc/MoorFaserWerk_Malchin_Kurzexpose_v1.pdf

title: Germany – Load-bearing structure design services – Planungsleistungen Tragwerksplanung gemäß HOAI, Teil 4, Abschnitt 1, §51 für die Maßnahme Neubau/Anbau: Kindergarten Renquishausen
description: Die Gemeinde Renquishausen plant den Neubau eines 4-gruppigen Kindergartens in der Ortsmitte, angrenzend an das Gemeindezentrum. Das Grundstück befindet sich in stadträumlich anspruchsvoller Hanglage. Der zweigeschossige Neubau nutzt die Höhenentwicklung für ebenerdige Zugänge in beiden Geschossen. Der Neubau bindet über einen eingeschossen Zwischenbau mit Dachterrasse an die bestehende Gemeindehalle an.

title: Finland – ENT or audiologist services – Kuulokojeiden sovitus- ja huoltopalvelut ÖVPH Pohjoinen alue
description: Hankinnan kohteena on kuulokojeiden sovitus- ja ylläpitopalvelu Pohjanmaan hyvinvointialueen pohjoisella osa-alueella. Palveluun sisältyy lääkinnällisenä kuntoutuksena myönnettyjen kuulokojeiden sovitus ja ylläpitopalvelu sekä muiden yksittäisten korvakappaleisiin ja kuulokojeisiin liittyvien huoltotoimenpiteiden hankinta kaudelle 1.1.2027 - 31.12.2028. Hankintaan sisältyy kaksi kertaa yhden (1 + 1) vuoden optiomahdollisuus (1.1.2029-31.12.2029 ja 1.1.2030-31.12.2030). Option käyttämisestä tehdään erikseen päätös noin kuusi (6) kuukautta ennen sopimuskauden päättymistä. Toiminta-alue on Pohjoinen alue, johon kuuluu Pietarsaari, Kruunupyy, Luoto, Pedersöre ja Uusikaarlepyy. Pietarsaaren alueella on noin 250 kuulonhuoltoasiakasta per vuosi. Asiakasmäärä on arvio eikä tilaaja sitoudu tiettyihin hankintamääriin. Palvelun asiakkaalla on oltava palvelua varten korva-, nenä- ja kurkkutautien toimintayksikön toimintaperiaatteiden mukaisesti hyväksytty lähete tai apuvälinepäätös, jonka määräysten mukaan kuulokojepalvelu toteutetaan. Tilaaja varaa oikeuden tarkastella palvelun järjestämistapaa sopimuskauden aikana. Tarkastelun seurauksena palvelun laajuus voi muuttua tai palvelu voidaan osittain tai kokonaan siirtää tilaajan omaksi toiminnaksi hankintasopimuksen ehtojen mukaisesti.

title: Finland – Lift-maintenance services – Oulun Tilapalvelut - Hissien huolto- ja korjauspalvelut
description: HANKINNAN KOHDE Oulun Tilapalvelut -liikelaitos pyytää tarjoustanne hallinnoimiensa kiinteistöjen hissien huolto- ja korjauspalveluista sekä hälytyskeskuspalveluista. Hankinnan kohteena ovat hissien kokonaisvaltainen huolto-, kunnossapito-, korjaus- ja päivystyspalvelu. Palveluun sisältyvät lisäksi hissien toiminnan ylläpitämiseksi tarvittavat muut huolto- ja korjaustoimenpiteet. Palvelun tavoitteena on varmistaa hissien turvallinen, luotettava ja keskeytyksetön toiminta sekä ylläpitää laitteiden tekninen kunto valmistajien ohjeiden, viranomaismääräysten ja hyvän kunnossapitotavan mukaisesti. Hankinnan tarkempi sisältö on kuvattu tämän tarjouspyynnön liitteessä 1 (Palvelunkuvaus). Lisäksi liitteessä 2, (Laiteluettelo / Tarjousliite) on kerrottu jokaisen hissin vaadittu huoltomäärä vuodessa. SOPIMUSJÄRJESTELY Hankinnasta muodostetaan puitejärjestely yhden (1) palveluntuottajan kanssa. TOIMEKSIANTOJEN TOTEUTUS Perushuollot toteutetaan sovitun huolto-ohjelman mukaisesti. Kiireettömien töiden tilaukset tehdään P2P-tilausjärjestelmällä, joka toimii samalla tilauksen sopimuksena. Tilauksen yhteydessä sovitaan toimeksiannon sisältö, aikataulu sekä arvioitu työmäärä. Mikäli sovitusta aikataulusta myöhästytään palveluntuottajasta johtuvasta syystä, tilaajalla on oikeus periä sopimusluonnoksen mukaiset sanktiot. HINNOITTELU JA TARJOUKSEN SISÄLTÖ Tarjous tulee laatia tämän tarjouspyynnön ja sen liitteiden mukaisesti. Tarjouksen tulee kattaa kaikki palvelun toteuttamiseksi tarvittavat työt. Mahdolliset lisätyöt hinnoitellaan tarjouspyynnön mukaisesti. Perushuollot laskutetaan laitekohtaisilla tarjoushinnoilla. Muut huolto- ja korjaustyöt laskutetaan tarjotun tuntihinnan sekä toteutuneen materiaalikulutuksen mukaisesti. SOPIMUSKAUSI Sopimuskausi on kaksi (2) vuotta. Sopimuskauden tavoiteltu alkamispäivä on 1.12.2026. Mikäli sopimuskauden aloitus viivästyy esimerkiksi muutoksenhaun vuoksi, sopimuskausi alkaa vasta, kun asiaan on saatu lainvoimainen ratkaisu. Määräaikaisen sopimuskauden jälkeen sopimusta voidaan jatkaa optioilla: - yksi (1) + yksi (1) vuotta Optiokaudet alkavat tavoitellusti: - 1.11.2028 (1. optiovuosi) - 1.11.2029 (2. optiovuosi) Tilaaja päättää optioiden käytöstä. Sopimus jatkuu optiokausille automaattisesti, ellei tilaaja ilmoita kirjallisesti halustaan olla käyttämättä optiota viimeistään kuusi (6) kuukautta ennen kunkin optiokauden alkamista. HISSIEN LISÄÄMINEN JA POISTAMINEN Sopimuskaudella hankinnan kohteet voivat lisääntyä tai vähentyä ja tilaajalla on oikeus lisätä tai poistaa kohteita sopimuksesta ilman irtisanomisaikaa. Lisättyihin ja poistettuihin kohteisiin sovelletaan tarjouksen mukaisia hintatasoja. TAKUUAIKAISTEN HISSIEN HUOLTOVASTUU Tämä hankinta ei koske takuuaikaisia huolto- ja korjauspalveluja. Takuuaikaiset hissit pysyvät toimituksesta tai hissin korjauksesta vastanneen toimittajan huollossa takuuajan päättymiseen saakka. Takuuajan päätyttyä huolto- ja korjausvastuu siirtyy tämän sopimuksen mukaiselle palveluntuottajalle. Tilaaja ilmoittaa palveluntuottajalle takuuajan päättymisajankohdan. SOPIMUSEHDOT JA HANKINTAPÄÄTÖS Palvelussa noudatetaan JYSE 2025 -ehtoja. Tilaajalla on oikeus hylätä kaikki tarjoukset perustellusta syystä. Tarjoukset eivät saa sisältää tarjoajan omia ehtoja. HANKINNAN KÄYTTÄJÄT Sopimusta voivat käyttää Oulun Tilapalvelut -liikelaitoksen lisäksi myös muut Oulun kaupungin hallintokunnat ja liikelaitokset, joilla on sama Y-tunnus, kuten Oulun Kaupunkiympäristöpalvelut ja Oulun Vesi.

Contract Duration: The contract period will be from the date of contract to 2030-03-31 Solicitation Method: Competitive Number of Contracts: One (1) Comprehensive Land Claim Agreement Applies: No Applicable Trade Agreements: The requirement is subject to the provisions of the World Trade Organization Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO-AGP), the Canada-Chile Free Trade Agreement (CCFTA), the Canada-Peru Free Trade Agreement (CPFTA), the Canada-Colombia Free Trade Agreement (CColFTA), the Canada-Panama Free Trade Agreement (CPanFTA), the Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), Canada Korea Free Trade Agreement (CKFTA), Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), Canada-Honduras Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Ukraine Free Trade Agreement, Canada-United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement (Canada-UK TCA) and the Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA). Requirement Details Tendering Procedure: Selective Tendering This requirement is open only to those TBIPS Supply Arrangement Holders who qualified under Tier 1 for services in the National Capital Region for the following categories: • Category A.1. Application/Software Architect Level 3 • Category I.2. Database Administrator Level 3 • Category I.6. Network Analyst Level 3 • Category I.11. Technology Architect Level 3 The following SA Holders have been invited to submit a proposal: • Accenture Inc. • ADRM Technology Consulting Group Corp. • BoonBridge Corporation • CDW Canada Corp. • CGI Information Systems and Management Consultants Inc. • Cofomo Inc. • Deloitte Inc. • Donna Cona Inc., IBM Canada Limited Joint Venture • Flex Tech Services Inc • Primex Project Management Limited • Prologic Systems Ltd., and Maplesoft Consulting Inc. in JV • Skyfly Solutions Inc., iFathom Corp., EPI-Use Now Inc. in Joint Venture • Spaghetti Logic Inc. • TRM Technologies Inc. • Xelerance Corporation Description of Work: The objective of this requirement is to augment knowledge within the Department of Justice Canada’s (JUS) Cloud team to gather expertise and meet project requirements and specific AI initiatives. The required professional services will support the delivery of key infrastructure components, networking fixes and improvements as well as high visibility projects such as Otto , Artificial Intelligence and the Lakehouse. The Cloud Engineer will implement, configure, automate, and support cloud infrastructure, platform services, and cloud-native solutions in accordance with Government of Canada Cloud Guardrails, departmental standards, enterprise architecture principles, and security controls. The Cloud Engineer will support the deployment, integration, modernization, and operational management of Microsoft Azure services, enterprise applications, AI-enabled solutions, and hybrid cloud environments. The Cloud Engineer will collaborate with the Cloud Centre of Expertise (CCoE), Shared Services Canada (SSC), Security Operations, infrastructure teams, application teams, and project stakeholders to deploy, configure, monitor, troubleshoot, automate, and document cloud services, platform components, application hosting environments, identity services, storage, networking, and operational processes while supporting continuous improvement, operational excellence, and knowledge transfer. The Cloud Architect will design, document, and provide technical leadership for the Department's cloud architecture, ensuring compliance with Government of Canada Cloud Guardrails, departmental standards, security controls, and enterprise architecture principles. The Cloud Architect will support cloud infrastructure, cloud-native applications, application modernization initiatives, Azure platform services, AI-enabled solutions, and hybrid architectures. Responsibilities include the design of governance models, subscription hierarchies, landing zones, security architecture, integration patterns, DevSecOps practices, application hosting models, and reference architectures to support enterprise cloud adoption and integration with on-premises and cloud-based services. The Network Specialist will design, implement, document, and support cloud and hybrid networking solutions that provide secure, resilient, and high-performing connectivity between cloud, on-premises, partner, and externally hosted environments. The specialist will support enterprise cloud platforms, cloud-native applications, application modernization initiatives, AI-enabled solutions, and hybrid architectures by designing and implementing networking services, secure integration patterns, and connectivity solutions. The Network Specialist will collaborate with Shared Services Canada (SSC), internal Security Operations, infrastructure teams, application teams, and project stakeholders to design, implement, validate, and document network connectivity, firewall configurations, DNS services, certificate management, identity integration, private connectivity, and network security controls in accordance with Government of Canada standards and departmental policies. The Database Administrator will design, implement, maintain, and optimize database platforms across on-premises and Azure environments, ensuring the availability, performance, security, and recoverability of business-critical systems. The Database Administrator will implement and support backup, restore, high availability, disaster recovery, monitoring, and security controls, while providing technical advice and documentation related to database migrations, cloud integration, and operational best practices in coordination with application teams, Shared Services Canada (SSC), and internal security stakeholders. Bidders must submit a bid for all resource categories. Security Requirement: All Contractor personnel must hold at a minimum, a Personnel security screening level of Reliability. Privileged users require a Personnel Security screening level of Secret. Unscreened personnel are prohibited from performing services under the Contract. Minimum Corporate Security Required: Reliability Minimum Resource Security Required: Secret Contract Authority Name: Ryan Greig Phone Number: 437-295-5631 Email Address: Ryan.Greig@justice.gc.ca Inquiries Inquiries regarding this RFP requirement must be submitted to the Contracting Authority named above. Request for Proposal (RFP) documents will be e-mailed directly from the Contracting Authority to the Qualified Supply Arrangement Holders who are being invited to bid on this requirement. BIDDERS ARE ADVISED THAT “BUYANDSELL.GC.CA” IS NOT RESPONSIBLE FOR THE DISTRIBUTION OF SOLICITATION DOCUMENTS. The Crown retains the right to negotiate with any supplier on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language. NOTE: Task-Based Informatics Professional Services (TBIPS) Method of Supply is refreshed three (3) times per year. If you wish to find out how you can be a “Qualified SA Holder”, please contact RCNMDAI.-NCRIMOS@pwgsc.gc.ca

description: Important Note: The closing date for the initial RFSA solicitation period is the date posted on page 1 of the RFSA Document. This requirement is for the Department of Fisheries and Oceans (DFO). Title: Request for Supply Arrangement – Ghost Gear The Department of Fisheries and Oceans Canada has a requirement to establish Supply Arrangements for crews and vessels capable of retrieving and appropriately disposing of ghost gear in Canadian waters when the need arises. DFO’s retrieval requirement might be different every time ghost gear is reported due to the conditions, location, sensitive habitats and gear type. DFO does not know the specific requirements until the location and gear is observed. • Retrieval activities may include: mapping capacity (ie. Side scan sonar or similar) to identify targets • Retrieval (by various methods including but not limited to: by hand from vessel, commercial diver, remotely operated vehicle (ROV), barge and excavator). • Transportation to disposal location which may require a boat, barge, truck, etc. • Disposal, including recycling when appropriate PERIOD OF THE SUPPLY ARRANGEMENT The resulting Supply Arrangement will have no defined end-date and will remain valid until such time as Canada no longer considers it to be advantageous to use it. SECURITY There is no security requirement for this contract. Suppliers working under this Supply Arrangement must not be given access to sensitive information or assets, and must be escorted at all times while on DFO premises. TRADE AGREEMENTS This requirement is subject to the Canada-Chile Free Trade Agreement (CCFTA), Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), Canada-Colombia Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Peru Free Trade Agreement (CPFTA), Canada-Panama Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Korea Free Trade Agreement (CKFTA), Canada–Ukraine Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Honduras Free Trade Agreement, Canada-United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement, World Trade Organization–Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO-GPA), and the Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA). Suppliers’ arrangements must clearly demonstrate that they meet all Mandatory Requirements for the proposal to be considered for further evaluation. Arrangements not meeting the mandatory criteria will be excluded from further consideration. Mandatory Criteria M1 The Supplier must have experience in one or more of the following: 1. surveying 2. retrieving ghost gear from in water 3. transporting ghost gear 4. responsibly disposing of ghost gear 4. Returning of identifiable gear IMPORTANT NOTICE on Insurance Requirements: At the Request for Proposal (RFP) stage, the Offeror will be required to provide valid certificates of insurance demonstrating that the insurance coverage applicable to the nature of the work is in place and maintained. title: Refrigeration and HVAC Services at the Pacific Biological Station (PBS), Nanaimo, British Columbia (B.C.).
description: BACKGROUND INFORMATION Canada is seeking offers from Offerors to provide refrigeration and HVAC maintenance and repair services to the Pacific Biological Station (PBS) of the Department of Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO) located in Nanaimo B.C. Canada intends to issue up to two (2) Standing Offers. Compliant offers will be ranked in ascending order according to their total evaluated price. The compliant offer with the lowest evaluated price will be ranked first, and the compliant offer with the second-lowest evaluated price will be ranked second. Canada may issue fewer than two Standing Offers if fewer than two compliant offers are received. SCOPE OF WORK The Contractor must provide all labour, materials, tools, equipment, supervision, and travel necessary to deliver refrigeration and HVAC maintenance and repair services on an as-and-when-requested basis by means of a Call-up against the Standing Offer at the Pacific Biological Station (PBS), Nanaimo, British Columbia, for the Department of Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO). All work must be performed in accordance with the applicable federal and provincial codes, regulations, and standards listed under the References section of this standing offer. Where discrepancies exist between codes, the most stringent requirement applies. A. Services Services required under this standing offer include, but are not limited to: a. Assembling pipe sections, tubing, and fittings using couplings, clamps, screws, bolts, cement, plastic solvent, caulking, soldering, brazing, and welding equipment; b. Filling pipes or HVAC fixtures with water or air and observing pressure gauges to detect and locate leaks; c. Servicing glycol heating and cooling loops; d. Servicing and installing boilers (steam and condensing) and associated equipment; e. Servicing rooftop units, heat pumps, and hydronic heating systems; f. Servicing heat exchangers; g. Reviewing blueprints, building codes, and specifications to determine work details and procedures; h. Preparing written cost estimates for labour and materials prior to commencing work (see Section 7 — Scheduling); i. Studying building plans and inspecting structures to assess material and equipment needs, establish pipe installation sequences, and plan installations around obstructions such as electrical wiring; j. Maintaining records of all assignments and producing detailed work reports; k. Performing calculations and planning for complex or large-scale jobs; l. Locating and marking positions of pipe installations, connections, passage holes, and fixtures using precision measuring instruments including rulers and laser levels; m. Measuring, cutting, threading, and bending pipe to required angles using hand and power tools, including pipe cutters, pipe-threading machines, and pipe-bending machines; n. Installing pipe assemblies, fittings, and valves for all HVAC equipment; o. Cutting openings in structures to accommodate pipes and pipe fittings using hand and power tools; p. Hanging steel supports from ceiling joists (concrete, steel, or wood) to hold pipes in place; q. Repairing and maintaining HVAC equipment, including replacing defective components, mending or replacing broken pipes, and clearing clogged drains; r. Directing workers engaged in pipe cutting, preassembly, and installation of plumbing systems and components; and s. Supplying and installing stainless steel, ABS, and PVC piping, valves, and associated fixtures for HVAC equipment. B. Equipment Equipment covered under this standing offer includes, but is not limited to: • Distribution piping systems: PVC, ABS, steel, stainless steel, copper, cast iron, PEX, and flexible steel-braided; • Water and glycol circulation pumps; • Sump pumps; • Valves: ball, gate, butterfly, globe, pinch, disc check, and equivalent types; • Safety valves associated with the ammonia refrigeration system; • Glycol heating loop equipment; • Boilers: steam and condensing; • Rooftop units, heat pumps, and hydronic heating systems; • Air compressors; • Air dryers; and • Heat exchangers. CALL-UP PROCEDURES – RIGHT OF FIRST REFUSAL 1. Call-up by Authorized Representative. The Identified User’s authorized representative places a Call-up under the Standing Offer for goods, services, or both included in, and at the prices and in accordance with the terms and conditions specified in, the Standing Offer. 2. Multiple Standing Offers. Call-ups will be issued using a right of first refusal basis: The call-up procedures require that when a requirement is identified, the Identified User will contact the highest-ranked offeror to determine if the requirement can be satisfied by that offeror. If the highest-ranked offeror is able to meet the requirement, a call-up is made against its standing offer. If that offeror is unable to meet the requirement, the identified user will contact the next ranked offeror. The identified user will continue and proceed as above until one offeror indicates that it can meet the requirement of the call-up. In other words, call-ups are made based on the “right of first refusal” basis. When the highest-ranked offeror is unable to fulfill the need, the identified user is required to document its file appropriately. The resulting call-ups are considered competitive and the competitive call-up authorities can be used. LOCATION OF WORK Pacific Biological Station, Nanaimo, British Columbia. Services will be provided at a multi-building research campus comprising laboratories, office buildings, aquaculture facilities, refrigeration systems, and associated infrastructure. STANDING OFFER PERIOD The period for issuing Call-ups and providing services against the Standing Offer is from Standing Offer issuance to the date that is five (5) years thereafter (the “Expiry Date”), inclusive. TRAVEL AND LIVING EXPENSES Canada will not pay any travel or living expenses associated with performing the Work. SECURITY REQUIREMENTS There are no security requirements associated with this solicitation of offers or the Standing Offer; however, security requirements may be applicable at the time of issuance of Call-ups. Trade Agreements This procurement is subject to the provisions of the Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA), the World Trade Organization Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO-GPA), the Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), the Canada-United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement (CUKTCA), and other applicable trade agreements.

title: Design, Installation, Maintenance and Support of Electronic Security Systems
description: Given the evolving threat environment both in Canada and internationally, NRCan is focused on strengthening the physical security posture of its facilities. This includes improving access control, surveillance, and intrusion detection capabilities to ensure personnel safety and operational continuity. NRCan operates an electronic security and surveillance system consisting of access control, video management, and intrusion detection systems deployed across multiple locations nationwide. The system is maintained through a combination of in-house IT and security resources, as well as contracted security system support and integration services. The system transitioned from legacy analog infrastructure to an IP-based architecture between 2016 and 2020, with ongoing enhancements through 2023. The current security system is built on a hybrid cloud and on-premises architecture, designed to balance cost and performance with confidentiality, integrity, and availability requirements. The system includes approximately 500 card readers and 500 cameras across more than 25 sites and is monitored through the NRCan Security Operations Control Centre (SOCC) located at 580 Booth Street in Ottawa, Ontario.

title: Netherlands – Transport services (excl. Waste transport) – Deelbakfietsen Ede
description: De Gemeente Ede wenst de exploitatie van deelauto's in Ede-Centrum en elektrische deelbakfietsen in de hele Gemeente Ede in de markt te leggen middels concessies. Met deze concessies beoogt de Gemeente een kwalitatief, toekomstbestendig en toegankelijk aanbod van deelauto’s en elektrische deelbakfietsen te realiseren, passend bij de ruimtelijke ontwikkeling van het centrumgebied en de mobiliteitsopgaven van de Gemeente. In verband met de verschillende markten en de verschillende concessiegebieden voor deelauto’s en elektrische bakfietsen kiest de Gemeente ervoor om deze concessies middels twee aanbestedingen uit te vragen: één voor elektrische deelbakfietsen en één voor deelauto's. Deze aanbesteding betreft de aanbesteding elektrische deelbakfietsen. De opdracht betreft de concessie voor de exploitatie van elektrische deelbakfietsen in de Gemeente Ede. De concessie wordt uitgevoerd binnen drie regimes: • Regime 1: basisaanbod deelbakfietsen in Ede-Centrum binnen het werkingsgebied Mobiliteitsfonds (zoals weergegeven in Bijlage 2); • Regime 2: het behouden van aanbod van deelbakfietsen op 14 reeds bewezen locaties. • Regime 3: organische uitbreiding in de rest van Ede;

title: France – Guard services – 26.741.01 SÉCURISATION DES LOCAUX ET GESTION A DISTANCE PAR TELESURVEILLANCE DES SITES DE LA CAISSE PRIMAIRE CENTRALE D’ASSURANCE MALADIE DES BOUCHES-DU-RHONE
description: Lot N°1 - SÉCURISATION RECURRENTE DES LOCAUX DE LA CPCAM DES BOUCHES-DU-RHONE ET SECURISATION PONCTUELLE : Pour le lot n°1, il est attendu : - La sécurisation des agents, des assurés et le contrôle d’accès de neuf sites comprenant le Centre Administratif de Valmante et huit agences par la mise à disposition d’agents de sécurité sur les sites concernés ; - La sécurisation ponctuelle à la demande en cas d’évènements exceptionnels, hors sécurisation à la demande énoncée dans le lot 2, concernant l'ensemble des sites. Il s’agit ici d’assurer la sécurité des agents et des assurés en cas d’évènements exceptionnels pouvant porter atteinte à leur intégrité physique (ex : grèves, manifestations externes et internes, agressions verbales et /ou physiques dans l’une des agences, etc …) Lot N°2 – GESTION DE LA SECURITE DES SITES DE LA CPCAM DES BOUCHES-DU-RHONE PAR TELESURVEILLANCE, INTERVENTIONS ET GARDIENNAGE D’URGENCE Pour le lot n°2, il est attendu : - La gestion à distance concernant l'ensemble des sites par télésurveillance ; - La gestion des interventions suite à un déclenchement d’alarme ou à la demande de la CPCAM des Bouches-du-Rhône ou d’un appel extérieur concernant l'ensemble des sites (levée de doute) ; - Gardiennage d’urgence à la demande concernant l’ensemble des sites (limitée à 4 semaines maximum). Il s’agit ici d’assurer le gardiennage des bâtiments suite à une intervention ayant relevé un risque pour celui-ci (ex : intrusion, dysfonctionnement, faille sécuritaire, etc) Les missions relevant du présent accord-cadre doivent permettre d’assurer la sécurité incendie, de surveiller l’accès aux locaux des sites, de prévenir, intervenir, et contrôler toute action suspecte sur le site, accueillir, renseigner, secourir tout individu en difficulté.

title: Travel Management Office (TMO) Travel Program (Defense Travel System (DTS) & Government Travel Charge Card (GTCC)) and Mail Management Center (MMC) Technical and Administrative Support Services.
description: This is a SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE (SSN) announcement. SSNs are issued to assist the Agency in performing market research to determine industry interest and capability. No proposals are being requested or accepted with this synopsis. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR PROPOSALS AND NO CONTRACT SHALL BE AWARDED FROM THIS SYNOPSIS. In accordance with (IAW) Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 10, SSP is conducting market research to determine if sources are capable of successfully performing the requirements identified in this SSN. title: Netherlands – Engineering services – Overeenkomst ingenieursdiensten civieltechnische werken gemeente Bergeijk
description: De opdracht bestaat uit het uitvoeren van ontwerp, (project) engineering, project (bege-)leiding en ondersteuning binnen cultuur – en civieltechnische projecten. Hoofdonderdelen: het verrichten van ontwerp werkzaamheden bij herinrichtingen met (burger)participatie het verrichten van cultuur- en civieltechnisch tekenwerk; het bepalen van hoeveelheden t.b.v. bestekvoorbereiding; het realiseren van RAW bestekken inclusief bijlagen; het schrijven van de nota’s van Inlichtingen; controleren winnende offertes; het houden van toezicht en directie; advieswerkzaamheden op het gebied van verkeer, stedenbouw, landschapsarchitectuur, bestratingen en milieu; ondersteunende werkzaamheden bij trajecten met (burger)participatie; het begeleiden van door derden uit te voeren onderzoeken; overige werkzaamheden indien van toepassing. Het betreft ingenieursopdrachten met een geschatte waarde tot € 100.000,- exclusief btw per deelopdracht. De uit te voeren werkzaamheden liggen binnen de gemeentegrenzen van de gemeente Bergeijk en vallen onder haar verantwoordelijkheid. De gemeente zou voor iedere deelopdracht een separate aanbesteding kunnen doorlopen. Echter gezien de waarde van de deelopdrachten wordt juist gekozen om deze onder te brengen in een raamovereenkomst, zodat dit de doelmatigheid van opdrachtverstrekking ten goede komt. Hierdoor is er sprake van een samengevoegde opdracht. De inschrijvers kunnen de werkzaamheden zonder of met een gering aantal onderaannemers uitvoeren: zij hebben doorgaans alle disciplines in huis. Splitsen in percelen die onafhankelijk van elkaar kunnen worden gegund, leidt niet tot een betere toegankelijkheid voor het mkb, maar tot extra activiteiten en dus meer inefficiëntie en dus meer kosten. De opdracht is als geheel toegankelijk voor het mkb. Daarom wordt er geen perceelindeling toegepast waarbij de percelen onafhankelijk van elkaar kunnen worden gegund. De opdrachtgever gaat met twee partijen een overeenkomst aan. De opdrachten worden evenredig op basis van omzet verdeeld. De overeenkomst wordt aangegaan voor een periode van minimaal twee jaar en maximaal zes jaar. De ingangsdatum van de overeenkomst is 1 februari 2027.

title: Civilian Armored Vehicle Manufacturers
description: Civilian Armored Vehicle Manufacturers NOTICE: The purpose of this notice is for information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation. OVERVIEW The U.S. Department of State is conducting market research to identify qualified sources capable of providing civilian armored vehicles. This Sources Sought Notice requests information from civilian armored vehicle upfitters and manufacturers to assist in acquisition planning. NAICS Code: 336211 � Motor Vehicle Body Manufacturing Small Business Size Standard: 1,000 employees PURPOSE This Sources Sought Notice seeks to identify potential vendors that specialize in civilian armored vehicles. The Government will only accept responses from firms that perform the actual armoring work from start to finish. Responses from brokers or intermediaries will not be accepted. MANUFACTURING LOCATION REQUIREMENT All vehicle armoring work under any resultant contract shall be performed at facilities located in the United States. The resultant contract will not allow the Contractor to perform or subcontract any armoring work to facilities located in countries subject to U.S. sanctions or export control restrictions. ANTICIPATED CONTRACT DETAILS Contract Type: Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Period of Performance: One (1) year base period plus nine (9) twelve-month option periods INFORMATION REQUESTED Interested parties should provide the following information in their response: 1. Company Information a. Company name b. Company address c. Point of contact (POC) name, phone number, and email address d. DUNS number (or UEI if transitioned) 2. Small Business Status a. Indicate whether your company is a small business under NAICS code 336211 b. If applicable, list the socioeconomic category in which your company belongs (e.g., 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, WOSB) 3. SAM Registration a. Confirm that your company is registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) i. Provide SAM UEI number 4. Capability Statement (20-page maximum), focusing on your firm's ability to armor various types of passenger vehicles: a. Armoring Experience � Provide details of vehicle armoring experience in the private and/or public sectors for the previous 10 years, including: i. Types of vehicles armored; make, model, and model year going back no further than 10 years. ii. Example use cases of past vehicles armored (e.g., cargo transport, VIP protection). iii. Ballistic and blast protection levels achieved for standards such as NIJ, VPAM, STANAG, etc., and any non-standard protection requirements met. iv. Fabrication capability for opaque armor materials, and types and thicknesses of materials used in previous armored vehicles. v. Client references (if releasable). b. Contract Volume and Track Record i. Total dollar value of vehicle armoring contracts/orders performed annually over the past 3 years. ii. Largest single order (by vehicle quantity and dollar value) completed within a 12-month period. c. Manufacturing Capabilities i. Location(s) of manufacturing facility/facilities. ii. Any subcontractors used in vehicle production. iii. Production capacity in vehicles per year. iv. Current production lead time, from contract/order award to delivery, for a single vehicle and for a batch order (e.g., 10, 25, 50 vehicles). v. Surge capacity: ability to increase production temporarily to meet urgent Government requirements, and associated timelines. vi. Quality certifications (e.g., ISO, industry-specific certifications). 5. Facility Security Clearances a. Details regarding current and/or past facility security clearances (e.g., FCL level and expiration date) 6. GSA Schedule (if applicable) a. GSA Schedule number b. Period of performance 7. Acquisition Strategy and Contract Structure Feedback a. Does your firm have experience performing under an IDIQ contract with multiple 12-month option periods? If so, please describe. b. Would your firm be able to compete effectively if this requirement is set aside for small business, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, or WOSB concerns? Please explain any concerns with a small business set-aside. c. Based on your knowledge of the industry, are you aware of at least two other capable, responsible small businesses that could perform this requirement? (This helps the Government assess set-aside feasibility under the Rule of Two.) d. Would your firm prefer or recommend a single-award IDIQ or a multiple-award IDIQ for this requirement? Please explain the rationale. e. Do you have experience with, or a preference for, Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) task/delivery orders versus other pricing arrangements (e.g., FFP with economic price adjustment) for this type of work, given potential material cost volatility (e.g., steel, ballistic glass, composites)? f. What is a reasonable Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) cost range per vehicle for common armoring configurations (e.g., B4/B6 level sedan, B7 level SUV), if you are able to share this for planning purposes? g. Are there minimum order quantities or dollar thresholds your firm would require to make individual task orders economically viable? h. What is your firm's standard warranty period and terms for armoring work performed, including coverage for parts, labor, and any workmanship defects? i. Is your firm capable of providing warranty support at U.S. Department of State posts located overseas? If so, please describe how this support would be delivered, including: Delivery method � e.g., dispatch of traveling technicians from the U.S. or a regional hub, use of vetted local subcontractors/service partners, or a combination of both; Coordination with post � how your firm would coordinate with the post's General Services Office (GSO) or Facilities Management team to schedule access, obtain necessary country clearances, and comply with local security and customs requirements; Response times � anticipated timeframes for initial response and on-site arrival, accounting for post location (e.g., high-threat vs. standard posts) and regional logistics; Parts and logistics � how replacement parts or materials would be sourced and shipped to the post, including any customs, or import/export control considerations; and Limitations � any posts, regions, or security environments where your firm would be unable to provide direct warranty service, and what alternative arrangements (e.g., remote technical support, depot-level repair) would apply in those cases. j. Does your firm have bonding capacity sufficient to support a multi-year IDIQ of this size? If comfortable sharing, please indicate your bonding capacity or capacity range. k. Would your firm be interested in, or already positioned for, teaming or subcontracting arrangements with other firms to meet the full scope of this requirement? l. Are there any customer-furnished vehicle chassis considerations (e.g., Government-furnished base vehicles vs. contractor-procured) that would affect your proposed approach or pricing? m. Do you foresee any barriers (e.g., export control licensing, material sourcing, facility capacity) that could limit competition or timely performance under this requirement? SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS Deadline: Responses must be received no later than 11:00 AM EST on October 13, 2026. Submission Method: All responses, including attachments and any questions regarding this Notice, should be submitted electronically to: Maria Anguiano: anguianom@state.gov Wanda I. Cruz: cruzwi@state.gov Subject Line: Sources Sought Response � Motor Vehicle Body Manufacturing

RTX Corporation (Pratt & Whitney), General Electric Aerospace (GE-A), and Rolls-Royce Corporation are the original equipment manufacturers (OEM) for the engines affected, and as such, are the only firms that possess the necessary knowledge, experience, and technical data required to perform these efforts. THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. No solicitation is available. However, any firm that believes it is capable of meeting this requirement must respond in writing with clear and convincing evidence to support their ability to provide timely and effective services. This documentation must be submitted within fifteen (15) days of this publication. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement or to proceed on a sole source basis. A determination by the Government not to compete this action based on responses received is solely within the discretion of the Government. The antcipated award date is 29 October 2027. title: Ireland – Radioactive-, toxic-, medical- and hazardous waste services – Collection and Disposal of Category 1 Waste from Dublin Airport Passenger Terminals and Airside Stables
description: Due to the risk of introducing diseases into the European Union (EU) from third countries, there are strict rules and regulations around animal products and plants and plant products entering the EU. Any products that are prohibited from entry are seized and disposed of as Category 1 waste. Prohibited products in passengers’ luggage on airplanes poses a very particular risk to public, animal and plant health, resulting in its disposal being strictly regulated. Accordingly, there are controls are in place to ensure that seizures of prohibited food or plants at Dublin Airport is controlled and disposed of in a manner that minimises risk to public, animal and plant health. Past outbreaks of diseases (e.g. Foot and Mouth Disease) demonstrate the risks posed by products of animal origin, animal by-products (ABP) and plants being introduced to Ireland through travel. The successful tenderer will be responsible for the removal, emptying, cleaning and disinfection of the Department of Agriculture, Food and Marine bins at following locations in Dublin Airport: • Terminal One • Terminal Two • Airside Stables It must be noted the successful tenderer must be registered to land Category 1 waste under Article 23 of Regulation (EC) 1069/2009 and must be registered prior to commencing operations. The operator must also ensure to abide by all relevant requirements set out in national (SI 187 2014) and EU Legislation (Regulations 1069/2009 and 142/2011). Full details in Notice titled CN25ALander, published with the tender documents. Also please note there are Terms and Conditions from Dublin Airport Authority that the successful tenderer must comply with to operate at the airport, please refer to "Dublin Airport Authority miscellaneous charges booklet 2026" published with the tender documents.

title: Trade and Cargo Academy
description: **Note: The sources sought originally posted as W912HP27RA001 - Due to technical issues with ACWS a new solicitation number was pulled. The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Charleston District (SAC) has a new requirement for construction of a Trade and Cargo Academy at the Federal Law Enforcement Training Center (FLETC). The requirement will include hazardous material abatement and selective demolition of the current vacant 30,000 SF, three-story building, while preserving the existing main lobby and ensuring uninterrupted utility service to the occupied east wing. In its place, a new 28,400 SF, two-story, flood-resilient facility will be constructed. Due to poor soil quality and its location within FEMA Zone AE, the TCA will use a deep precast concrete pile foundation with pile-supported slabs, a heavy-duty steel frame to withstand high wind/seismic demands, a modern rainscreen envelope, and fully integrated building systems (HVAC, LED lighting, and security infrastructure). The interior will have space for instructional use on the first floor (including classrooms, an auditorium, and production spaces) and administrative open offices on the second floor. FLETC also has a requirement for the construction of a new Cargo Security and Seized Property Training Facility (CSSPTF), a separate one-story 5,985 SF facility purpose-built to support U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) training. Specifically designed for hands-on vehicle/cargo inspection, evidence processing, and simulated seized property storage, this site-adapted facility will also be elevated on a deep pile foundation to comply with stringent floodplain requirements. A key engineering focus for this site is the implementation of pile-supported stormwater piping under paved areas to mitigate soil settlement risks. Both facilities are engineered for a minimum 40-year operational lifespan, integrating highly durable, low-maintenance coastal materials, and will comply fully with the latest federal energy conservation standards, DHS security criteria, and 2021 building codes. These facilities are essential for the increased student enrollment and additional courses offered supporting FLETC Charleston.

title: Technical Services
description: This Special Notice is to advise interested members of the Training and Readiness Accelerator II (TReX 11), as well as other interested members within the U.S. technology base, that a Request for Solutions (RFS) has been issued by Advanced Technology International (ATI) for Future Training Directorate (FTD) The purpose of the Training and Readiness Accelerator II (TReX II} is to spur innovative development, demonstration, and expedited delivery of prototypes to increase Warfighter readiness via modeling, simulation, education/training, experimental validation, and military readiness focused projects. A consortium has been established to develop prototypes directly relevant to enhancing the mission effectiveness of military personnel and the supporting platforms, systems, components, or materials proposed to be acquired or developed by the Department of Defense (DOD), or to improvement of platforms, systems, components, or materials in use by the Armed Forces. Link for TREX Il-https://www.trexii.org/ This prototype project will enhance the mission effectiveness of military personnel by improving the platforms, business systems and business procedures within the Future Training Directorate (FTD). The contractor shall collect, analyze, and archive data that will support programmatic, business initiative requirements, develop and maintain related study databases and/or websites formatted for multiple toolsets, including scenario laydowns and system representations utilized within analytic tools for participation in joint experimentation, initiatives and other analysis forums. The contractor shall support the Government by assisting and performing integrated analysis, evaluations and/or assessments of organizational structures, missions, architectures with relevant analysis to include for prototyping, modeling and simulation, concepts for the realm of the possible, services, products, systems, and technologies in the areas of doctrine, organization, training, materiel, leadership and education, personnel, facilities, and policy (DOTMLPF-P).

title: Upgrade Water Tanks - FCI Texarkana, Tx
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for the project titled Upgrade Water Tanks at the Federal Correctional Institution in Texarkana, Texas. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. The Federal Bureau of Prisons (FBOP) intends to make a single award to a responsible entity that will provide all materials, labor, and equipment to complete the project in accordance with the Statement of Work and Drawings. This will be a firm fixed price construction contract. SCOPE OF WORK: The contractor shall restore and modernize FCI Texarkana�s water storage and distribution system. This includes complete rehabilitation of the 1,000,000?gallon ground water tank and 150,000?gallon elevated water tower, replacement of all pumps, piping, valves, and hardwired control panels, and installation of a fully air?gapped analog monitoring system. All work must meet AWWA, NFPA, OSHA, NEC, and federal security requirements, followed by comprehensive testing, certification, and a 5?year system warranty. The performance period for the project will be 336 Calendar Days from issuance of the notice to proceed. The estimated magnitude of the project lies between $1,000,000.00 and $5,000,000.00. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code applicable to this requirement is 237110 with a corresponding small business size standard of $45 million. To be considered an interested vendor, you must possess this NAICS code in your System for Award Management (SAM) registration. This is a 100 percent small business set-aside. You must be registered in www.sam.gov as a small business for the applicable NAICS code (see FAR provision 52.219-1 in the Representations & Certifications section of your sam.gov registration. The solicitation will be distributed solely through the Contract Opportunity website at https://www.sam.gov. Hard copies of the solicitation will not be made available. The website provides download instructions. The "Sensitive /Secure package Upload" option will be selected for this procurement. All secure/locked documents uploaded, to include the solicitation, will require an active SAM vendor registration to obtain access. In addition, only those vendors who have been issued a valid Marketing Partner Identification Number (MPIN) from www.sam.gov will be granted access. If your firm does not have the NAICS code listed in www.sam.gov required for this solicitation, an email may be forwarded to your firm requesting an explanation as to why your firm should be granted access. If you encounter problems accessing these documents, please contact the Federal Service Desk at 866-606-8220. All future information about this solicitation, including any amendments, will also be distributed solely through this website. Interested parties are responsible for continuously monitoring this website to ensure that they have the most recent information about this proposed contract action. IMPORTANT: Any contractor interested in obtaining a contract award with the Federal Bureau of Prisons must be registered in https://www.sam.gov. In order to qualify for award, your business size metrics information entered in your www.sam.gov SAM registration must be less than or equal to the size standard specified above. Each bidder's www.sam.gov registration will be reviewed by the Government to confirm that your business size meets the small business size standard requirement. All bidders are urged to double check their www.sam.gov registration and update as necessary, including the size metrics information. SITE VISIT (See Instructions to Offerors Attachment): An organized site visit has been scheduled for Wednesday, September 23, 2026 at 9:00 A.M., Local Time. Participants will meet at�FCI Texarkana, 4001 Leopard Drive, Texarkana, TX at the New Power House Parking Lot (Once you exit on to Leopard Drive, it will be the first yellow gate on your left.)

title: FORT PIERCE HARBOR MAINTENANCE DREDGING, ST. LUCIE COUNTY, FLORIDA
description: PROJECT DESCRIPTION: Project work includes maintenance dredging of Fort Pierce Harbor with excavated material being placed onto Fort Pierce Beach. Due to the extensive hardbottom areas located offshore of the fill area, offshore pipeline access to the beach site is prohibited. Offloading the beach fill will be done inside the South Jetty of Fort Pierce Inlet, as shown on the drawings. A staging area and beach access to the beach placement area are located at the end of Seaway Drive and near the south jetty pumpout location. Work also includes but is not limited to environmental and water quality monitoring, sea turtle trawl sweeping (hopper dredges only), screening, beach tilling, beach fill quality control, construction support, and vibration control and monitoring. Work will be divided into a base and two options. BIDS DUE: 13 October 2026 at 1:00 PM EDT. NAICS CODE: 237990, OTHER HEAVY CIVIL ENGINEERING CONSTRUCTION. SMALL BUSINESS SIZE STANDARD: $37 million. TARGET PRICE RANGE: Between $5,000,000.00 and $10,000,000.00. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: The Contractor shall be required to (a) commence work under this contract within SIXTY (60) calendar days after the date the Contractor receives the Notice to Proceed (NTP), (b) prosecute the work diligently, and (c) complete the entire work ready for use, and be off the beach, not later than 30 May 2027, with 30 June 2027 for the entire contract work. The time stated for completion shall include final cleanup of the premises. The completion date is based on the assumption that the successful offeror will receive the notice to proceed by 7 January 2027. The completion date will be extended by the number of calendar days after the above date that the Contractor receives the notice to proceed, except to the extent that the delay in issuance of the notice to proceed results from the failure of the Contractor to execute the contract and give the required performance and payment bonds within the time specified in the offer.

title: Demolition and Construction of Radio Tower at Mount Wachusett, Princeton, MA
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New England District is issuing a Sources Sought Announcement for Demolition and Construction of a Radio Tower at Mt. Wachusett, Princeton, Massachusetts. This announcement is to determine the interest, availability, and capability of 8(a), Women-Owned, Service Disabled Veteran-Owned, HUBZone and Small Business concerns for this project. The NAICS code for this procurement is 238910 with a size standard of $19M. The contract solicitation is planned to be issued in the spring of 2027 with construction to take place over a 4-month period beginning in the summer of 2027. The estimated construction cost is between $100,000 and $500,000. The radio tower on Mt. Wachusett facilitates radio transmission between multiple U.S. Army Corps of Engineers projects throughout New England. The tower also hosts antennas from several other agencies. The work of this project includes demolition of two (2) existing towers and construction of a new radio tower. The specific work includes site preparation, temporary removal of existing antennas, demolition of an 80 ft radio tower founded on rock and a 30-ft radio tower located on a radio building roof, construction of a self-supporting 90-ft radio tower, re-installation of the temporarily removed antennas, and replacement of the radio building�s rubber roof. The existing 80-ft radio tower is located within 10 feet of the radio building. Due to FAA permitting requirements, the proposed 90ft tower will be located in the same footprint as the existing tower. The contract site can be accessed via paved roads during the spring, summer, and autumn, but is closed during winter months. Interested firms should submit a capabilities package to include the following: business classification (i.e. HUBZone, etc.), type of equipment the firm might propose to use on the project, two (2) example projects performed by the firm in the last ten (10) years (including Points of Contact for those projects) showing experience with the project type and proposed equipment, and bonding capacity. Please indicate the team subcontractor(s) (if any), including their prior experience and qualifications meeting the same qualifications listed above, which will be used to support the bidder's effort. Firms may use subcontractor experience to demonstrate experience with the requirements, but the role and work performed by each team member (prime and subcontractors) on projects demonstrating that team member's experience shall be the same as the role for that team member for this project. Proof of bonding capability is required. Responses are limited to twenty pages and due by 13 October 2026. Responses should be emailed to: Distephano Marcellus distephano.marcellus@usace.army.mil Phone Contact: (978) 318-8890 The Government will not pay for any material provided in response to this market survey nor return the data provided. This notice is for information purposes only and is not a request to be placed on a solicitation mailing list nor is it a Request for Proposal (RFP) or an announcement of a solicitation. The results of this survey will be considered to be in effect for a period of one year from the date of this notice. description: September 23, 2026 The government is sitll working through RFI followup responses and the subsequent amendment. This amendment adjusts the proposal due date to 13 October, 2026, while the government finalizes documents. September 16, 2026 Complete RFI responses posted. Followup questions related to these RFIs can be submitted by September 21 at noon CST. The government is not accepting new questions. Any question submitted must be tied to an answer provided in the attachment. The proposal due date will remain unchanged but the government will continue to monitor the need to extend. September 3, 2026 Amendment posted with updated Proposal due date, please see attachment. The government is still working to answer all RFIs. August 25, 2026: See attachment for a complete list of RFIs received to date. Some have already been answered, and the government is working to answer the rest. The government will continue to evaluate the need to extend the proposal deadline based on the time required to answer all questions and supply those answers to industry. August 19 2026: Please see amendment 0002 attached and an updated Section L. August 11 2026: 1. Please see amendment 0001 attached and an updated Section L dated 5 August 2026. 2. The government is accepting RFIs until 21 August at 3PM EDT. If you have already sent your RFIs to the POCs you do not have to resubmit them. 4 August 2026: Please see the attached RFP (FA8137-26-R-0040) and all attachments. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- THIS POSTING WILL SATISFY THE REQUIREMENT OF RFO 5.101, Presolicitation Multiple Award Construction Contract (MACC) for General Construction Services will accomplish a broad range of sustainment, maintenance, repair, alteration/renovation, and minor construction projects affecting real property facilities at Tinker Air Force Base, Oklahoma. The work performed will be complex in nature, require multiple construction trades, and may require engineering design performed by credentialed professionals. Project execution methods will fall into one of the following classifications. The execution method will be defined in the project documents for each Task Order (TO) under this Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quanity (IDIQ) contract. Design Build will include the Contractor providing both the design and construction services for a project; during the Design-Build process, final design solutions are provided by the Contractor, not the Government. The Government will provide a Statement of Work (SOW), drawings, and other preliminary documents to establish requirements from the work to be completed. These documents will be equivalent to a schematic 15% or greater design. When awarded the TO for the project, the Contractor will complete the design to the 100% level to include drawings, specifications, design analysis/narrative, and other documentation as required by the Government. Construction with Limited Design method will include the Government providing the design and the Contractor will further develop portions as required and will provide construction services for the project. This method will be used for non-complex or repetitive work types of projects where design cost and effort is not warranted. The Government will provide the SOW, drawings, and other documents as necessary to establish requirements to complete the project. These documents will be equivalent to a design submittal 35% to 65%. When awarded the TO the Contractor will complete any additional design efforts required by the project and produce a set of working documents for use during construction. Construction only method will include the Government providing 100% design package, including the SOW, drawings, specification, and any other documents as necessary to establish requirements for the work to be accomplished. When awarded the TO the Contractor shall commence with construction in accordance with the design and contract requirements. The Contractor is required to furnish all materials, labor, plant, tools, transportation, equipment, testing services, quality control, and incidentals necessary to provide a complete useable end product as specified in the TO/project documents. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 236210, Industrial Building Construction with a small business size standard of $45 million. The MACC will be executed for one base period of five (5) years with one option period of five (5) years. The Government will negotiate equitable adjustments resulting from change orders in the shortest practicable time. Approximately 120 days are required to definitize equitable adjustments associated with change orders for construction. The definitization of an equitable adjustment begins when the contracting officer receives an adequate change order definitization proposal and ends when the contracting officer executes a contractual action to definitize the change order. title: Request for Information: Enterprise Training Infrastructure Project Scope Study and Feasibility Analysis
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) The Office of Acquisition Management (OAM), on behalf of the Office of the Chief Administrative Officer (OCAO), is requesting information from qualified Architectural & Engineering (A/E) firms regarding a potential business opportunity supporting future United States Capitol Police (USCP) enterprise training infrastructure planning. The United States Capitol Police recently completed a Training Facilities Requirements Assessment (TFRA) which evaluated the Department's current enterprise training infrastructure and identified operational capacity, throughput, concurrency, facility condition, and infrastructure limitations affecting the Department's ability to sustain current and future training requirements. Building upon the findings of the TFRA, USCP is seeking a qualified Architectural & Engineering (A/E) firm to conduct an Enterprise Training Infrastructure Project Scope Study and Feasibility Analysis. The purpose of the study is to further evaluate the validated operational requirements identified within the TFRA and develop feasible infrastructure alternatives capable of supporting the Department's current and future enterprise training mission. The study is expected to evaluate multiple infrastructure strategies that may include modernization or expansion of existing facilities, construction of new facilities, acquisition or leasing of facilities, utilization of partner agency resources, relocation of selected training functions, and hybrid approaches incorporating multiple infrastructure solutions. The resulting study will provide executive leadership with engineering, planning, operational, and financial information necessary to objectively evaluate infrastructure alternatives and formulate a preferred path forward balancing operational requirements, implementation realities, fiscal considerations, and future enterprise training demand. Please see the attached Statement of Objectives (SOO) for additional information regarding the proposed requirement. Submission Details Please submit the following documents to Linh.Williams@uscp.gov : Vendor Capability Statement addressing the attached Statement of Objectives (SOO). Description of the firm's experience conducting comparable Architectural & Engineering feasibility studies, infrastructure planning efforts, campus planning initiatives, or comparable federal, military, law enforcement, or public safety facility planning projects. A recommended technical approach for accomplishing the objectives identified within the SOO. A recommended scope of services, anticipated deliverables, multidisciplinary team composition, and recommended Period of Performance (POP). A Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) budgetary estimate for the proposed effort. OAM is also interested in any recommendations vendors may have to improve the proposed requirement, study methodology, acquisition strategy, or future Statement of Work. Questions & Answers Please submit all questions in writing to Linh.Williams@uscp.gov using the Attachment B - Questions and Answers Template. USCP responses to contractors' questions will be provided as an attachment to this RFI notice and amended throughout the open period of this posting, as needed. It is the responsibility of the contractor to check this posting for updates. Terms of this Request The purpose of this Request for Information (RFI) is to collect additional information regarding the subject requirement and identify the willingness and capabilities of potential vendors to support the proposed effort. This RFI is issued solely for information or planning purposes and does not constitute a Request for Quote (RFQ). The information provided in this RFI is subject to change and is not binding on the Government. USCP has not made a commitment to procure the services discussed herein, and release of this RFI should not be construed as a commitment or authorization to incur costs for which reimbursement would be required or sought. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. The USCP does not have authority to enter into contracts for architecture and engineering services or construction. The responses obtained from this RFI and any subsequent solicitation will be used to inform decision makers and stakeholders in Congress, the Legislative Branch, and partner agencies.

Weld filler materials shall be clearly identified and segregated from each other both when in storage and at the work station. Work station environment shall be controlled to prevent conditions adverse to proper gas shielding. 3.9 CLEANING. Parts to be welded shall be cleaned to remove surface soils such as oils, waxes, grease, inks, etc. except that uninhibited alkaline solutions such as sodium hydroxide shall NOT be used. 3.10 DEOXIDIZING. The cleaned parts shall be chemically deoxidized NO MORE THAN 10 DAYS PRIOR TO WELDING to remove thick surface oxide films. (If the material or work is exposed to an outdoor environment, this time limit shall be reduced to a maximum of 3 days, to account for atmospheric effects.) Mechanical cleaning methods shall be applied just prior to the actual start of welding, to remove any reoxidation or residual thin oxide films. 3.10.1 CHEMICAL TREATMENT. An acid deoxidizing treatment shall be applied by either immersion or brushing/wiping. Deoxidizers acceptable for use shall include nitric acid, sulfuric chromic, phosphoric chromic, or equivalent solutions. Sodium hydroxide solutions shall not be used. Care shall be taken to assure 100% solution coverage of the area to be welded. To allow an adequately sized deoxidized area for good welding, the solution shall be applied to an area extending at least 2 inches from the weld site, or ending at any closer adjacent edge. 3.10.2 MEC

N4008526R0178 This acquisition is being solicited on an unrestricted basis with full and open competition. THIS SOLICITATION INCLUDES CMMC LEVEL 1 (SELF) REQUIREMENTS IN ACCORDANCE WITH DFARS 252.204-7025 (DEVIATION 2026-0038) AND 252.204-7021 (DEVIATION 2026-0038). This project is considered a �Large-scale Construction Project� as defined in FAR 22.502 (DEVIATION 2026-O0040). Accordingly, the requirements of FAR Subpart 22.5 (DEVIATION 2026-O0040) will apply. The Offeror shall submit a signed Project Labor Agreement with their Price Proposal submission, in accordance with FAR Provision 52.222-33 (DEVIATION 2026-O0038) and FAR Clause 52.222-34 (DEVIATION 2026-O0038). Offerors that do not include a signed Project Labor Agreement complying with the terms of FAR 52.222-33 (DEVIATION 2026-O0038) and 52.222-34 (DEVIATION 2026-O0038) shall be considered nonresponsive and ineligible for award. Description of Work: This design-bid-build project will include the construction of a multi-story steel frame 12,920 SF laboratory and office facility. The facility will support a variety of functions including depot level testing of critical torpedo systems. Construction consists of a steel frame building with a shallow foundation, metal standing seam roof and masonry and metal panel exterior walls. The project includes all pertinent site preparations and site improvements, including underground stormwater retention system, mechanical and electrical utilities, telecommunications, landscaping, drainage, parking and exterior lighting. For Option 1, P1016 Consolidated RDT&E Systems Facility, this project will include the construction of a multi-story 17,978 SF laboratory facility supported by shallow foundations. The facility will utilize structural steel framing with a standing-seam roof. Exteriors are planned as a combination of masonry veneer and metal panel siding. Demolition includes removal of Building 1272T, a 548 m2 engineering facility.

description: 08/28/2026 Update: The attachment titled, "Amend 0001 Attachment B - Questions and Answers" provides the Government's responses to contractors' questions. REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) The Office of Acquisition Management (OAM), on behalf of the Office of the Chief Administrative Officer (OCAO), is requesting information from qualified Architectural & Engineering (A/E) firms regarding a potential business opportunity supporting future United States Capitol Police (USCP) enterprise training infrastructure planning. The United States Capitol Police recently completed a Training Facilities Requirements Assessment (TFRA) which evaluated the Department's current enterprise training infrastructure and identified operational capacity, throughput, concurrency, facility condition, and infrastructure limitations affecting the Department's ability to sustain current and future training requirements. Building upon the findings of the TFRA, USCP is seeking a qualified Architectural & Engineering (A/E) firm to conduct an Enterprise Training Infrastructure Project Scope Study and Feasibility Analysis. The purpose of the study is to further evaluate the validated operational requirements identified within the TFRA and develop feasible infrastructure alternatives capable of supporting the Department's current and future enterprise training mission. The study is expected to evaluate multiple infrastructure strategies that may include modernization or expansion of existing facilities, construction of new facilities, acquisition or leasing of facilities, utilization of partner agency resources, relocation of selected training functions, and hybrid approaches incorporating multiple infrastructure solutions. The resulting study will provide executive leadership with engineering, planning, operational, and financial information necessary to objectively evaluate infrastructure alternatives and formulate a preferred path forward balancing operational requirements, implementation realities, fiscal considerations, and future enterprise training demand. Please see the attached Statement of Objectives (SOO) for additional information regarding the proposed requirement. Submission Details Please submit the following documents to Linh.Williams@uscp.gov : Vendor Capability Statement addressing the attached Statement of Objectives (SOO). Description of the firm's experience conducting comparable Architectural & Engineering feasibility studies, infrastructure planning efforts, campus planning initiatives, or comparable federal, military, law enforcement, or public safety facility planning projects. A recommended technical approach for accomplishing the objectives identified within the SOO. A recommended scope of services, anticipated deliverables, multidisciplinary team composition, and recommended Period of Performance (POP). A Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) budgetary estimate for the proposed effort. OAM is also interested in any recommendations vendors may have to improve the proposed requirement, study methodology, acquisition strategy, or future Statement of Work. Questions & Answers Please submit all questions in writing to Linh.Williams@uscp.gov using the Attachment B - Questions and Answers Template. USCP responses to contractors' questions will be provided as an attachment to this RFI notice and amended throughout the open period of this posting, as needed. It is the responsibility of the contractor to check this posting for updates. Terms of this Request The purpose of this Request for Information (RFI) is to collect additional information regarding the subject requirement and identify the willingness and capabilities of potential vendors to support the proposed effort. This RFI is issued solely for information or planning purposes and does not constitute a Request for Quote (RFQ). The information provided in this RFI is subject to change and is not binding on the Government. USCP has not made a commitment to procure the services discussed herein, and release of this RFI should not be construed as a commitment or authorization to incur costs for which reimbursement would be required or sought. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. The USCP does not have authority to enter into contracts for architecture and engineering services or construction. The responses obtained from this RFI and any subsequent solicitation will be used to inform decision makers and stakeholders in Congress, the Legislative Branch, and partner agencies.

(2) Critical and major welds may be subjected to further non destructive testing (such as dye penetrant inspection)as prescribed by the buying activity. (3) Proper documentation shall be available for review by Government personnel. 3.6 WORK INSTRUCTIONS. Work instructions shall be posted at theoperator's work station giving procedures to control the welding process, i.e., filler material, weld size, electrical and gas characteristics, including flow rate. 3.7 MATERIALS AND MATERIALS CONTROL. The quality program shall assure that the materials used in fabrication or processing, i.e., base metals and weld filler material, be inspected and conform to the applicable physical, chemical and other technical requirements (supplier's certification is sufficient). 3.8 CONTROLS. Weld filler materials shall be clearly identified and segregated from each other both when in storage and at the work station. Work station environment shall be controlled to prevent conditions adverse to proper gas shielding. 3.9 CLEANING. Parts to be welded shall be cleaned to remove surface soils such as oils, waxes, grease, inks, etc. except that uninhibited alkaline solutions such as sodium hydroxide shall NOT be used. 3.10 DEOXIDIZING. The cleaned parts shall be chemically deoxidized NO MORE THAN 10 DAYS PRIOR TO WELDING to remove thick surface oxide films. (If the material or work is exposed to an outdoor environment, this time limit shall be reduced to a maximum of 3 days, to account for atmospheric effects.) Mechanical cleaning methods shall be applied just prior to the actual start of welding, to remove any reoxidation or residual thin oxide films. 3.10.1 CHEMICAL TREATMENT. An acid deoxidizing treatment shall be applied by either immersion or brushing/wiping. Deoxidizers acceptable for use shall include nitric acid, sulfuric chromic, phosphoric chromic, or equivalent solutions. Sodium hydroxide solutions shall not be used. Care shall be taken to assure 100% solution coverage of the area to be welded. To allow an adequately sized deoxidized area for good welding, the solution shall be applied to an area extending at least 2 inches from the weld site, or ending at any closer adjacent edge. 3.10.2 MEC

title: Coordinated SECREP Management and Strategic Logistics Services (CSM_SLS)
description: MARCORLOGCOM provides globally responsive ground equipment inventory control and integrated operational-level logistics capabilities in order to maximize Marine Corps materiel readiness and sustainment. As part of this mission, the Marine Forces Storage Command (MFSC) CSM Program provides logistical augmentation to the Marine Corps Reparable Issue Point(s) (RIP) located at I, II, and III MEF, as well as MFR in support of the CSM program, which is detailed in MCO 4400.200A. Additionally, the MFSC CSM Program performs strategic level CPI in consonance with the Logistics Modernization Solution Initiating Directive (LSMID) that outlines anticipated Realignment of Supply (ROS) outcomes for SECREP management. Finally, the MFSC CSM Program performs strategic level supply chain management, coordinated retail management, and logistics services planning for the Marine Corps, which makes up the Strategic Logistics Services (SLS) portion of this requirement. This is a small business set-aside for SeaPort-NxG MAC holders.

title: Mobile & Data Services for the U.S. Embassy Panama
description: The U.S. Embassy in Panama requires mobile and data services, including voice and text for basic phones and unlimited data service for Smart Phones and Tablets, for official domestic and international use. The anticipated performance is for a base year, with two one-year option periods, if exercised by the Government. The U.S. Government intends to award a contract to the most qualified, responsible offeror representing best value using trade-off evaluation methodology. The Embassy intends to conduct a pre-quotation conference, and all prospective quoters are invited to attend. Prospective offerors should contact Aranza Gutierrez at (507) 317-5309, or by email to PNMPROCREQ@state.gov for additional information or to arrange access to the virtual meeting. Quotations are due by 3:00p.m. on Tuesday, October 13th, 2026. No quotations will be accepted after this time. Quotations must be in English and incomplete quotations will not be accepted. Your quotation must be submitted electronically to PNMPROCREQ@state.gov . It is important to make sure the submission is made in specific size and format; in MS-Word 2007/2010 or MS-Excel 2007/2010 or Adobe Acrobat (pdf) file format. The file size must not exceed 30MB. If the file size should exceed the 30MB, the submission must be made in separate files and attached to separate emails with less than 30MB each. In order for a quotation to be considered, you must also complete and submit the following: 1. SF-1449 2. Section 1, Pricing 3. Section 5, Representations and Certifications 4. Additional information as required in Section 3 5. The Offeror shall submit a completed IRS Form W-14, found at www.irs.gov/w14, to ensure compliance with FAR 52.229-11. 6. Proof of SAM Registration. 7. CYBERSECURITY SUPPLY CHAIN RISK MANAGEMENT (C-SCRM) C-SCRM Questionnaire and/or State Department Secure Software Development Attestation Form Direct any questions regarding this solicitation in writing to Alex Phannestiel, Contracting Officer. Questions must be written in English and may be emailed to PNMPROCREQ@state.gov or sent to fax number (507) 317-5141 no later than COB Monday, September 21, 2026. Notwithstanding FAR 4.203-1(b)(5)(ii), the Contracting Officer has determined that it is in the best interest of the U.S. Government that offerors be registered in the SAM (System for Award Management) database at https://www.sam.gov at the time of submitting a proposal.
